question: Ticket ba777080011b says 'bin_shortcuts must read instance bin and class bin as separate directories and merge them; the two bins are not implicitly unified through symlinks', but outline 5.4.3.3.1 reads "A new shortcut needs no watch. Most instance bins are links to their class bin, so the shortcut is reachable the moment its file lands; the build's proof is the whole guarantee. Akien 2026-11-09, answering Q#75: "why the hell would it need a heartbeat?"" (Outline asserts 'Most instance bins are links to their class bin, so the shortcut is reachable the moment its file lands' — this mechanism assumes symlinks unify the bins without needing explicit separate reads. The ticket's approach either contradicts this factually (if symlinks don't exist) or adds unnecessary complexity (if they do). These cannot both be the intended architecture.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: Both stand; they do not contradict. Measured 2026-11-10: of the ten instance bins under ~/.cairn/devices, six are links and every link points at cairn/devices/<device>/0/bin, never at the bin/ beside the device's code (cairn/devices/<device>/bin/). The one such bin, cairn/devices/cairn/bin/ (start, stop, restart), is reached by no link: ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/bin is a plain directory. 5.4.3.3.1 says a new shortcut needs no watch, which holds: the launcher (30366e99655a) runs the bin beside the code by reading it directly, as this ticket has the list do. The two reads are the same two folders the launcher already runs.
